heroHeadline: Mount Jack Fire Near Sooke Grows to 276 Hectares as NWT's Active Count Collapses to Just 7 Fires
heroSubtitle: The out-of-control Mount Jack wildfire west of Sooke, BC grew to 276 hectares by September 24 and was determined human-caused, with heavy smoke over Greater Victoria grounding helicopter bucketing for parts of the day; roughly 60 personnel remain assigned and no evacuation orders or alerts have been issued. It is now one of only two fires still classified out of control across all of British Columbia, whose active count has fallen to 100 from 105 two days earlier. The Northwest Territories' season has effectively wound down — its active fire count collapsed from 79 to just 7 (5 out of control, 2 under control) as 282 of its 289 season fires are now declared out. Ainslie Creek near Merritt grew modestly to 69,705 hectares while remaining held. No new deaths or evacuation orders were identified this cycle.
